text:
maria: thinking out loud — i'd like an SDK header to let SRE/support simulate routing decisions for debugging customer issues. e.g. force route to dedicated pool or to eu region. safe by default, gated for admin tokens. thoughts?

alex: +1 for a header. what do you want it to control exactly? region only or also tier/variant and fallback behavior?

maria: region + tier + fallback-policy. example headers: `X-Redwood-Region: eu-west1`, `X-Redwood-Tier: gold`, `X-Redwood-Fallback: allow-lighter|no-fallback|regional-only`. SDK would expose a `routeHint` option too.

sasha: we need strong guardrails: headers must only be honored when caller has support debug/scoped permission. otherwise it's a DoS/cost exploit. also decide whether this should change billing/quota semantics.

ryan: agree on permissions. also think about telemetry: we should emit a `routing.debug_hint` event with fields `hint_type`, `requested_tier`, `effective_route`, `fallback_applied` so console can show simulated vs actual.

alex: telemetry is critical. console should have a waterfall for routing decisions per request id. useful for postmortems. we already collect route decisions but not the hint origin. add `hint_origin` = sdk|console|policy

maria: UX idea: in console rollout page, allow "simulate hint" for a customer that shows what would happen (no real routing changes). toggle shouldn't consume quota. separate checkbox "apply to live traffic" to actually change routing.

sasha: small nit — if simulate path doesn't consume quota we must be sure it won't interfere with cache or warm-up metrics. prefix/kvcache might get warmed and skew metrics. maybe route simulator should be cold-only or mark simulated requests in telemetry so we can filter warming.

ryan: good point. mark simulated requests `x-redwood-simulated: true` internally and exclude from billing/cost dashboards. also add `simulated=true` tag in traces.

maria: quick cURL example for what i'm prototyping:

```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west1" -H "X-Redwood-Tier: gold" -H "X-Redwood-Fallback: allow-lighter" -H "X-Redwood-Debug: route=simulate" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```

alex: SDK surface should mirror that, e.g. `client.generate({input, routeHint: {region:'eu-west1', tier:'gold', fallback:'allow-lighter'}, debug:{simulate:true}})`

sasha: about fallback: we need deterministic priority lists per customer and per model family. If `allow-lighter` triggers, we should pick the highest-quality compatible variant available in the target region/tier. we must log the full variant chain that was attempted.

ryan: agree. for service impl: compute candidate variants -> apply capacity checks -> pick first available -> if none, then apply cross-region fallback if policy allows -> if still none return a clear 503 with `x-redwood-fallback: none` metadata. include `variant_priority` in response headers.

maria: question on quotas: if support forces route to gold but customer is on silver plan, should we bill as gold? my leaning: if it's an admin-forced live change (not simulate), count as the actual variant used (gold). but console should show an audit reason.

alex: sounds right. but add rate-limits preventing accidental expensive routing in bulk — e.g., support can only route N requests/min with override unless an opt-in escalation flag is set.

sasha: also: we should avoid letting SDK header override internal tenant isolation. i.e., if customer is pinned to dedicated pool for compliance, header cannot move them out. headers must be constrained by policy evaluation.

ryan: implemented policy check list: 1) permission check 2) tenant policy compatibility 3) quota/cost guardrails 4) variant availability -> apply fallback per `X-Redwood-Fallback`. we can emit `routing.decision` event with `policy_violations` if denied.

maria: can infra-bot dump a sample routing event proto so i can wire telemetry?

infra-bot: deploy: routing-service v2.5.1 is live in staging. sample event JSON posted to #eng-platform-ops (link) : `routing_decision:{request_id, tenant_id, hint:{region,tier,fallback}, decision:{variant,region,reason}, simulated:false}` :shipit:

alex: one more thing — SDK should expose opt-in debug headers only when a `debugMode` flag is enabled at client init, so accidental shipping of debug headers in prod apps is unlikely.

maria: sounds like an action list. i'll draft an RFC with: header contract, permission model, telemetry events, console simulate UI flow, quota semantics, and sample SDK + curl snippets. assigning to me to draft, will ping for reviews. :eyes:

sasha: thanks — please include a small e2e test plan (simulate, forced fallback, policy deny, quota accounting).

ryan: +1 — add dashboard queries for `routing.debug_hint` and `routing.decision` joins so SREs can run retros on misroutes.

maria: filing RFC now, will link here when ready.

infra-bot: note: rolling deploy currently at 35% traffic for v2.5.1 in prod, no errors reported.
